clue.text: A newspaper looks into immoral practices in clergymen's homes

indicators.note: to look into something is to go inside it, so the newspaper piece sits within the vices

parts.note: vices are immoral practices
rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid investigates scandalous goings-on in the houses of the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks into' reads as investigating, but it signals going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a parish vicar, one kind of clergyman.

clue.text: List of words accountant entered in very old book

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it, so the accountant goes within the other letters

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper's name has been written into an ancient volume's word list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered in' puts CA between O and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocab, short for vocabulary, is a list of words, as in a language learner's glossary.

clue.text: Queen and king first welcomed in distant land

indicators.note: a guest welcomed in is taken inside, so the king and first go within the land

parts.note: China is a far-off country
R is short for rex, Latin for king
1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A monarch and his heir are received in a faraway country.
explanation.walkthrough: First as 1ST, with the digit read as the letter I, is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina was a seventeenth-century reigning queen of Sweden.

clue.text: Nonconformist attitude will spell out curacy's end shortly

indicators.note: spelling out the letters in a fresh order signals they are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its s kept as a letter

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of end is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dissenting outlook will announce that a clergyman's post is soon to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims END to EN; 'will spell out' rearranges CURACYS plus EN into RECUSANCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Recusancy was the refusal to attend Church of England services, hence a nonconformist stance.

clue.text: Be reluctant to enter part of pool in storm?

definitions.text: Be reluctant to enter part of pool
definitions.meaning: to go off something is to stop liking it, and the deep end is part of a swimming pool
to storm is to rage or lose one's temper wildly

explanation.surface: A nervous swimmer hesitates to plunge into the deep water during bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'go off the deep end' means to turn against that part of the pool; as an idiom it means to fly into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper violently, which is what storming means.

clue.text: Nonsense poems ultimately below celebrity writer's standard

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means placed after the earlier pieces

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
George Sand was a French novelist; her name with the possessive s
tripe is rubbish or nonsense

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of poems

explanation.surface: Silly verse, in the end, falls short of the standard set by a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' puts TRIPE and S, the last letter from 'ultimately', under STAR + SANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the US flag, and a standard is a flag.

clue.text: Dispose of dog after a short time

indicators.note: after places the dog behind the short time

parts.note: mo is short for moment
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Get rid of the dog once a moment has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to finish off or deal with the remainder, disposing of it.

clue.text: Maybe copper confronted gangster

parts.note: met, as in met an opponent face to face
Al Capone was the famous gangster

explanation.surface: A policeman, perhaps, came face to face with a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like slang for a policeman, as the surface suggests, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is an example of a metal, as the 'Maybe' signals.

clue.text: Resentment as game finishes early

indicators.note: stopping before the end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: piquet is a card game for two players

explanation.surface: Bitterness sets in when the match ends before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes early' drops the last letter T from PIQUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or wounded pride, a form of resentment.

clue.text: British actor heard in this secluded spot

indicators.note: heard signals that the actor's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Donald Pleasence was a British film actor

explanation.surface: A famous British performer was spotted in this hidden-away corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns PLEASENCE, the actor Donald Pleasence's surname, into a word that sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasance is a secluded garden or pleasure ground attached to a grand house.

clue.text: Despicable sort I excluded from a farewell drink

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person

indicators.note: excluded from means the letter is removed from the word for farewell

parts.note: ciao is an Italian goodbye
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rotter was left out of the goodbye drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' takes I out of CIAO, leaving CAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Curaçao is an orange-flavoured liqueur from the Caribbean island of that name.

clue.text: Very old article, quite unusual

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of quite are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An ancient thing that is rather rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges QUITE to TIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique describes something old and valued for its age.

clue.text: Form of support is provided by degrees

parts.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some kind of backing comes from university qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided by' is a link: IS comes from, and joins, the degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is a foundation, the support on which something rests.

clue.text: Armed soldiers distributed rifles including dud one

indicators.note: including means the rifles take in the other letters
distributed means spread around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: US is short for useless, a dud
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Soldiers were handed out weapons, one of them defective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts US and I with RIFLES; 'distributed' rearranges the whole pool into FUSILIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusiliers were originally soldiers armed with a fusil, a light musket.

clue.text: Rule about air guns regularly ignored

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: ignoring every other letter keeps the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A regulation on airguns is routinely disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops A, R, U and S from AIR GUNS, leaving IGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch.

clue.text: Alpine factory producing confectionery

parts.note: rock is a hard stick sweet sold at British seaside resorts
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: A works turns out sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpine' as a noun means a mountain plant; ROCK is the hard sugar stick sold at British seaside towns.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpine is a plant of high mountains, the kind grown in a rock garden.

clue.text: Waiting to see execution taking place

parts.note: hanging is a form of execution
on, as in the show is on, means happening

explanation.surface: Someone lingers to watch a hanging being carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging on means waiting or holding out patiently.

clue.text: Mean to oust leader of insurgents from country beset by trouble

indicators.note: to oust is to expel, so a letter is removed
beset by means surrounded, so the trouble wraps the country

parts.note: ill means trouble or harm
Liberia is a West African country

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A plan to remove a rebel leader from a troubled nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning ungenerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal can mean ungenerous or stingy, a sense of mean.

clue.text: My grandfather originally joined Brit to cross the globe

indicators.note: the globe goes across between the other pieces
originally points to the first letter of grandfather

parts.note: limey is American slang for a Briton
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: Grandpa started out by teaming up with a fellow Briton to travel the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' as an exclamation of surprise is the definition, hidden at the start of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorblimey is a Cockney exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'.

clue.text: Cautious, approaching infernal place occupied by black monster

indicators.note: approaching places one piece just before the next

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
Dis is the classical underworld

explanation.surface: Wary of going near a hellish place in which a dark beast lurks.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm, in Dante a city of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Charybdis was the whirlpool monster of Greek myth faced by Odysseus.

clue.text: Ample lager supply

indicators.note: supply read as an adjective, supple or bendy, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: There is plenty of beer in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the anagram signal, read as 'in a supple way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and ample both mean of generous size.

clue.text: Old soldier crept through landing-stage

indicators.note: going through means passing inside, so the creeping word sits inside the pier

parts.note: a pier is a landing-stage for boats
stole, as in stole away quietly

explanation.surface: A veteran sneaked across the jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistoleer was a soldier armed with a pistol, a historical term.

clue.text: Notes audible to a certain degree

indicators.note: audible means what is heard, so the notes are spoken to give the answer's sound

parts.note: soh and fah are notes of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Musical tones can be heard up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' speaks SOH FAH, two notes of the sol-fa scale, giving the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: So far means up to a point or to a limited extent.

clue.text: An appeal for high-level support

parts.note: 'O' is the invocation that opens an appeal, as in a prayer
give, the plea that follows, as in 'O give thanks'

explanation.surface: Someone makes a plea for backing from the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The appeal is 'O give!', a plea in the style of a psalm.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogive is a pointed arch or diagonal vault rib, a support high in a building.

clue.text: Experience unhappiness on earth

definitions.meaning: to ... is to feel down, so to be in low spirits
here on earth, as opposed to heaven above

explanation.surface: A person suffers misery in this world.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as 'be low' for the first sense; the second is the old idea of earth lying beneath heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Here below is an old phrase for earthly life, set against heaven above.

clue.text: Cockney's bird is more expansive

indicators.note: a Cockney's accent turns the vowel sound of the word, so it is a spoken version

parts.note: a wader is a long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: An East Ender's girlfriend is broader.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, where 'wader' comes out sounding like this. 'bird' also suggests British slang for a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Wider means broader, more expansive.

clue.text: Broadcast A Fine Romance

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: fine and fair both describe good weather, so a fine is a fair

explanation.surface: A radio station plays the old song A Fine Romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' turns A FAIR, from 'A Fine', into a French-style word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An affaire is a love affair, a romance.

clue.text: Depression grips woman going round ancient monument

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the whole is read backwards
a hand that grips something closes around it, so the depression holds the woman inside it

parts.note: a dip is a hollow in the ground
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A feeling of gloom takes hold of a woman touring old sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' tempts as the definition of a mood, but it is the hollow. The single 'going round' turns the whole assembled container backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyramid is a great stone tomb of ancient Egypt, an ancient monument.

clue.text: Barrister sensibly covers brief

indicators.note: covers means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A lawyer wisely takes on a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like the barrister's case papers, but it is an adjective meaning short.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse and brief both mean short and to the point.

clue.text: I'll demonstrate CD briefly along with hi-fi equipment

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc
a player, such as a CD player, is hi-fi equipment

explanation.surface: A salesperson offers to show off a CD on the stereo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops C from DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: A displayer is one who displays, so the person speaking would demonstrate.
